title: Humanoid whole-body control adopts force-aware contact evaluation by H1 2027
body: Researchers at the Technical University of Munich released ThorArena, a benchmark that stress-tests humanoid whole-body control under deliberate, load-bearing physical contact - active force exchange, not collision avoidance. Capturing synchronized whole-body motion and hand forces from human operators across six contact-rich chores (lifting and lowering a water container, pushing and pulling a chair, and co-carrying an object with a partner), the team replayed those forces in simulation and scored policies with a Force-Aware Tracking Score that jointly grades tracking accuracy, robustness across force levels, control effort, and whether the robot stays upright to the end of the episode. The headline result is that force-informed evaluation exposes large performance gaps that stay invisible under conventional no-force testing, and only the authors' own Thor2 policy held near-perfect balance across all six tasks. Because Figure, Agility, and Boston Dynamics are pushing humanoids off pilot stages and into factories and warehouses - where a person will inevitably lean on, push, or hand something to the robot - the no-force motion-tracking demo is no longer sufficient evidence of readiness. I expect force-aware contact evaluation to cross from this single academic benchmark into commercial practice: by H1 2027 at least one leading humanoid platform, or an independent second group, publicly reports whole-body control results under active applied contact force rather than motion tracking alone.

reasoning.because: TU Munich's ThorArena finds humanoid whole-body controllers degrade once real contact forces enter
reasoning.given: Figure, Agility, Boston Dynamics push humanoids into factories where people physically contact them
reasoning.so_that: At least one leading humanoid platform or an independent group reports whole-body control under active contact force
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; ≥1 humanoid maker or group reports contact-force results
reasoning.plain_language: A new test pushes and leans on robots to see if they stay standing; today's best humanoids often fail, so makers will start testing this.

summary: TU Munich's ThorArena replays real human contact forces against humanoid whole-body controllers and finds leading policies degrade under load - gaps no-force testing hides. As humanoids move into factories, expect force-aware contact evaluation to reach a commercial platform by H1 2027.
